source.title: Efficient Training of Deep Neural Operator Networks via Randomized Sampling
source.authors: Sharmila Karumuri; Lori Graham-Brady; Somdatta Goswami

record.file_problem: The full paper text is supplied. It contains minor extraction artifacts in equations and symbols, but the relevant results and descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests randomized trunk-input sampling in DeepONet on three scientific operator-learning benchmarks and reports test-error outcomes, extending batch-size/generalization findings to this architecture and setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-error results for randomized sampling and its evaluation-point-count conditions. Cited results about large-batch training are background only and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses large-batch generalization findings to motivate randomized trunk sampling and evaluates its method on scientific operator regression. V5 names image classifiers and language models. These experiments vary output-location sampling while holding the input-function batch size at 256; they do not directly test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that random trunk-location sampling reduces training time while preserving or sometimes improving test accuracy, with a problem-dependent number of locations. Their explanation involving sharp minima is a proposed mechanism, not a measured result.
record.recipe_differences: Random trunk-point sampling during DeepONet training is compared with evaluating all available output points. This is a scientific operator-learning setting, not the natural-label classification setting in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of sampled evaluation points changes accuracy; the optimal number is described as problem-dependent. Randomly sampled versus uniformly spaced points also changes test error in the dynamical-system experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed epoch budgets, randomly evaluating intermediate numbers of output locations gives comparable or better held-out operator-regression performance than evaluating all locations; one location performs poorly in the dynamical-system task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomized output-location subsampling can preserve or improve DeepONet generalization on scientific operator-learning tasks, with a problem-dependent useful sample count.

fits_no_version.finding: Random location selection yields lower test MSE than uniformly spaced selection at matched counts of 5 and 10 locations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refreshing randomly sampled trunk locations can improve DeepONet test performance relative to uniformly spaced locations.

record.peer_reviewed: World Sci. Annu. Rev. Artif. Intell.
record.problems: Results are on three scientific operator-learning benchmarks, not the natural-label image or language tasks in V5. Most comparative test-error outcomes are described in prose alongside figures without numerical values in the supplied text; error bars or statistical tests are not stated. The paper attributes the gain to effective batch size but does not directly measure that mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: Training-time outcomes and loss-curve descriptions are not entered as separate rows because the version concerns held-out performance relative to training under batch-size changes; they are reported in Figures 4, 8, and 12 and discussed in Sections 3.1–3.3. Exact plotted test metrics are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Fixed-epoch batch-size penalties in image classifiers or language models and the specified recipe adaptations.
Dropout, weight decay, and augmentation comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Epochs are held fixed over input functions, and reducing Neval changes location exposure per update while preserving the number of updates for a given training-set size. The supplied figure text lacks readable individual plotted values, so the aggregate prose cannot establish condition-specific batch penalties. Poor performance at Neval = 1 does not itself qualify or contradict V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not studied.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures are not compared.
Adaptive optimizers are not compared with SGD or momentum.

The study varies the number of trunk evaluation points, affecting effective batch size, in DeepONet on three operator-learning tasks. It does not test fixed-epoch large-batch comparisons on image classifiers or language models, nor the listed adaptation recipes.
Dropout and weight decay are not varied.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures are not measured.
Memorized training examples are not identified or removed.

rows.subject: DeepONet
rows.operation_detail: Randomly sample trunk evaluation points during training; compare test error across evaluation-point counts.

conditions.value: dynamical system with random external force

rows.measure: Mean test R² and test MSE
rows.baseline: Neval = 100 corresponds to evaluating all available points
rows.value: Neval = 1 has notably poor accuracy; Neval = 10 or 50 gives comparable or better accuracy than Neval = 100.
rows.uncertainty: 10 independent runs with different seeds; no numerical error bar stated in the text.
rows.note: The result is stated for evaluation-point conditions collectively; exact plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Operator-regression sampling comparison falls outside V5. The row also combines multiple point counts and both test metrics; the prose does not distinguish comparable performance from improvement for each condition.
